# Chap02. Kubernetes의 설계 철학: # Chap02. The Design Philosophy of Kubernetes
> 16장 연재의 둘째 글입니다. Kubernetes의 설계 철학인 선언: > This is the second article in a 16-chapter series. We explore declarative configuration, control loops, and Watch-based communication, then connect these principles to the Kubernetes API and cluster architecture.
1장에서는 컨테이너와 Docker가 실행 환경을 일관되게 만드는 방법을: Chapter 1 explained how containers and Docker make runtime environments consistent. The exercise showed that starting a container still leaves work to do: restarting stopped containers, adding instances, and replacing images. Running containers and maintaining an application's operational state are different responsibilities.
Kubernetes는 사용자가 원하는 상태를 선언하면 실제 상태를 그 선: Kubernetes manages this work by bringing the actual state toward the state users declare. Before memorizing component names, it helps to understand how that declaration is shared and how differences from the actual state are reduced.
이번 글에서는 선언형, 제어 루프, 상태 변화 구독(Watch)이라는 세: This article introduces three design principles: declarative configuration, control loops, and subscriptions to state changes through Watch. We then examine how the API and cluster components implement those principles, and how a declaration results in running Pods. Finally, we compare the manual operations in Chapter 1 with Kubernetes commands.
Kubernetes는 **컨테이너 오케스트레이션**(Container O: Kubernetes is a **container orchestration** platform. Container orchestration automates placement, instance counts, recovery, and traffic distribution rather than merely starting containers. Kubernetes is an open-source platform that coordinates these operations across servers. [[1]](#ref-1)
2014년 공개된 뒤 전 세계 기여자가 코드를 쌓아 왔고, 주요 클라우드: Since its release in 2014, contributors around the world have developed it. Major cloud providers offer managed Kubernetes, and the same model can also run locally. A consistent operational approach across environments is one reason it has become a de facto standard.
Fig 2는 Kubernetes를 중심으로 배포 자동화, 모니터링, 네트: Fig 2 shows deployment automation, monitoring, networking, storage, and security tools around Kubernetes. Together, these tools provide the capabilities needed to operate applications beyond simply running them.
인기의 배경에는 이식성도 있습니다. Kubernetes를 전제로 만든 애: Portability also contributes to its popularity. Applications built for Kubernetes can use the same declarative approach when deployed in different environments. Operational tools integrate through these shared declarations and APIs.
그렇다고 배우기 쉽다는 뜻은 아닙니다. 처음에는 이름과 설정 파일이 많아: This does not make Kubernetes easy to learn. At first, the many names and configuration files can seem unnecessarily complex. With familiarity, attention shifts to what the platform can do. We will follow that progression through **motivation, design principles, core concepts, the path from declaration to execution, and command comparisons**.
이전 글에서 이미 느꼈듯, 컨테이너를 여러 개 실행하는 것 자체는 어렵지: As the previous article showed, starting several containers is not especially difficult. The harder part is **operational decisions and policies**. Docker standardizes runtime environments, and Dockerfiles record their construction as code.
```bash\n# Docker로 이미지를 만들고 실행하는 기본 흐름을:
```bash
# Recall the basic Docker image build and run workflow
docker build -t my-app:1.0 .
docker run -p 8080:80 my-app:1.0
```
같은 이미지로 로컬, 테스트, 운영 환경을 맞출 수 있게 되면서 환경 불: Using the same image locally, in testing, and in production greatly reduces environment mismatches. Compose groups containers into an application, and Swarm distributes them across servers. This raises a reasonable question:
“Docker Compose나 Docker Swarm으로도 충분하지 않은: “If Docker Compose or Docker Swarm is sufficient, why use Kubernetes?”
> Docker는 “컨테이너를 실행하는 도구”이고, Kubernetes는: > Docker runs containers; Kubernetes is an **orchestration platform** for managing the system in which containers run.
Fig 3의 왼쪽은 Docker의 컨테이너 실행에서 Compose의 단일: The left side of Fig 3 expands from running containers with Docker to configuring one server with Compose and operating multiple servers with Swarm. On the right, Kubernetes accepts declarations of desired state and operational policies, then performs placement and recovery against those criteria.
Compose나 Swarm으로 운영 요구를 충족한다면 Kubernetes: Kubernetes is not mandatory when Compose or Swarm meets the operational requirements. The distinction involves not only whether scaling is possible, but who decides when and how far to scale.
트래픽이 급증할 때 Swarm에서는 관리자가 직접 서비스 복제본 수를 늘: In Swarm, administrators often increase the service replica count manually when traffic rises.
```bash\n# Swarm에서는 확장을 사람이 직접 지시함을 보이는:
```bash
# Manually request scaling in Swarm
docker service scale web=10
```
확장은 가능하지만, **컨테이너를 언제 몇 개까지 늘리고 줄일지**의 판: Scaling is available, but a person decides **when to add or remove instances and how many to maintain**. Kubernetes can use a policy based on a condition such as CPU utilization, delegating subsequent scaling decisions and actions to the platform. For example, a policy can target increased capacity when CPU utilization exceeds 70%.
장애 복구도 운영 설정에 따라 달라집니다. Docker에서도 재시작 정책: Recovery also depends on configuration. Docker restart policies can restart exited containers on the same host, while Swarm maintains replicas across servers. Kubernetes divides container restart, replica maintenance, and node failure handling among its components. A single container exit and a whole-server failure follow different recovery paths.
배포 과정에서도 Pod를 점진적으로 교체하거나 이전 구성으로 되돌리는 정: Deployment policies can progressively replace Pods or restore an earlier configuration. More complex strategies, such as sending only part of the traffic to a new version, require routing components or additional deployment tools. It is important to distinguish built-in capabilities from those requiring extra configuration.
이처럼 운영 판단을 정책으로 남기려면, 사용자가 선언한 목표를 플랫폼이: Recording operational decisions as policies requires a platform that continuously checks the declared goal.
오케스트레이션을 “누가 무엇을 자동으로 하느냐”로만 보면 이름이 많아 보: Looking only at which component automates which task can leave a long list of names. Three principles provide a common thread for the concepts that follow.
A typical Docker command looks like this:
```bash\n# 명령형 실행: 지금 당장 기동하라고 지시하는 Dock:
```bash
# Imperative execution: start a container now
docker run -d nginx
```
이 명령은 “어떻게 실행할 것인가”를 지시합니다. 명령 자체가 실행 이후: It instructs the system how to start something now. The command itself does not keep managing its state afterward. This is an **imperative** approach.
Kubernetes에서는 원하는 상태를 보통 **YAML**(들여쓰기로: In Kubernetes, users commonly describe the desired state in **YAML**, a configuration format whose structure is expressed through indentation. A declaration submitted to the API is called a **manifest**. A **resource** is something managed through the Kubernetes API; a manifest is input for creating or changing it. A target of three replicas can be expressed as `replicas: 3`.
```yaml\n# 원하는 상태를 YAML 매니페스트로 남기는 예시\nr:
```yaml
# Record desired state in a YAML manifest
replicas: 3
```
The key is **desired state**: a statement of how things should be, rather than a report of what is running now. As with Compose YAML, the user records a goal and gives it to a platform. The difference lies in what the platform is responsible for after receiving it. [[2]](#ref-2)
Fig 4에서는 원하는 복제본 세 개와 현재 개수를 비교해 하나가 부족함: In Fig 4, the platform compares the desired count of three replicas with the current count, finds one missing, and restores the count to three. Desired state remains the comparison target after the startup command has finished.
한 번의 실행 방법을 지시하는 대신 “앞으로도 복제본 세 개를 유지한다”: Declaring “keep three replicas running” instead of specifying a one-time startup action is a **declarative** approach.
설정을 파일로 남기면 변경 내용을 검토하고 이전 설정과 비교하기도 쉽습니: Keeping configuration in files also makes changes easier to review and compare. A replica count change from three to five can be recorded in Git, showing who changed an operational setting. The updated declaration must then be submitted to the cluster; editing a local file alone does not change it.
**제어 루프**(Control Loop)는 실행 중인 **현재 상태**: A **control loop** repeatedly observes the **current state** and reduces its difference from the desired state. An individual corrective operation is called **reconciliation**.
제어 루프는 상태를 한 번 확인하고 끝내지 않습니다. 필요한 변경을 요청: A control loop does not stop after checking once. It requests a change and observes the result again, allowing it to discover new differences caused by failures or configuration changes. [[3]](#ref-3)
Fig 5에서 API에 기록된 원하는 개수는 세 개이고 현재 개수는 두: In Fig 5, the API records a desired count of three and a current count of two. The process managing replicas detects the difference, requests creation of the missing instance through the API, and observes the result again. Once a server is selected and the new replica starts there, the count returns to three. Automatically restoring state after a failure in this way is called **self-healing**.
복제본 개수를 관리하는 프로세스, 실행할 서버를 선택하는 프로세스, 컨테: Maintaining instance counts, selecting servers, and managing container execution are separate jobs. Their coordination is based on changes to shared state. A **Watch** subscribes a component to those changes.
왜 이렇게 만드는지는, **직접 호출**과 **공유 상태 + Watch*: Comparing **direct calls** with **shared state plus Watch** explains why this matters.
그림의 **직접 호출** 방식은 한 프로세스가 다음 프로세스를 호출해 작: With direct calls, one process hands work to the next by calling it. If the receiving process is down, the handoff must wait at that step.
**공유 상태와 Watch**를 사용하는 방식에서는 필요한 작업을 상태로: With shared state and Watch, work is recorded as state, and each process observes the changes relevant to its role. If the placement process stops, new placements must wait, but the recorded requests remain and can be processed after recovery. Other processes can continue managing work that is already running.
여기서 중요한 점은 모든 통신이 없어지는 것이 아니라, 앞 단계의 결과를: Communication does not disappear. Instead, each stage records its result in shared state for other components to observe. Kubernetes shares this information through the **API Server**, the interface for querying and changing state.
이제 상태를 공유하는 창구와, 각 작업을 담당하는 실제 구성요소를 살펴보: Next, we will examine that interface and the components responsible for each task.
앞에서 Docker, Docker Compose, Docker Swarm: Building on Docker, Compose, and Swarm, Kubernetes can be understood as a platform for **automating container operations across servers**.
Fig 7에서 사용자의 선언은 API Server를 거쳐 여러 Node로: In Fig 7, the user’s declaration passes through the API Server to a cluster containing several Nodes. This separates the API, the interface receiving requests, from the cluster, the environment in which workloads run.
첫째는 **API**입니다. API는 사용자가 클러스터에 “원하는 상태”: First is the **API**, the entry point for submitting desired state to a cluster. Requests such as “maintain three web containers” or “run this application image” go through the API. A common interface lets users request cluster operations without logging in to each server.
이 API에 요청을 보낼 때 사용하는 대표적인 도구가 **kubectl*: **kubectl** is the principal **command-line client** for this API. Querying or applying configuration in a terminal becomes an API request.
둘째는 **클러스터**(Cluster)입니다. 클러스터는 여러 컴퓨터를: Second is the **cluster**, the logical group of computers in which requests are carried out. Each participating server is a **node**. Like a Swarm cluster, Kubernetes treats multiple nodes as a group, with operational policies and automation layered on top. Users generally request a state for the cluster rather than specifying a particular server, even as nodes are added or removed. Managed cloud services can provide a cluster without requiring users to build it themselves.
실행 단위도 구분할 필요가 있습니다. Docker에서는 보통 **컨테이너: The execution unit also differs. Docker commonly operates on a single container. Kubernetes uses a **Pod**, a group of one or more containers placed and managed together, as its smallest deployable unit. Containers in the same Pod share its network and lifecycle. For now, remember that the cluster schedules and deletes Pods as units. [[4]](#ref-4)
그림의 두 컨테이너는 하나의 Pod에 속하므로 서로 다른 Node에 나뉘: The two containers in the illustration belong to one Pod and are not placed on different nodes.
그림처럼 한 Node에 여러 Pod가 배치되면, 각 Pod 안의 컨테이너: When multiple Pods run on a node, the container processes inside them use that server's CPU and memory.
매니페스트를 API에 제출하면, 플랫폼이 그 내용을 읽고 어느 노드에 앱: After a manifest is submitted, the platform determines where the application should run. Components use control loops to reduce the difference between desired and actual state. Whether an application is written in Node.js or Go, Kubernetes works with its image and manifest. A common API and declaration model across languages becomes especially useful as teams grow.
이제 API와 클러스터 뒤에서, **어느 서버에서 어떤 프로세스가 일을: We can now examine which processes run on which servers. We will begin with the **worker node**, where Pods execute, and then cover the **control plane**, which coordinates the cluster.
클러스터는 크게 **Worker Node**(워커 노드, 실제 Pod가: A cluster is broadly divided into worker nodes and control plane components.
Fig 8의 위쪽 Control Plane은 선언을 저장하고 필요한 작업: The control plane at the top of Fig 8 stores declarations and determines the required work. The worker nodes below run the containers in Pods. Their kubelet and kube-proxy processes also obtain information through the API Server. We will start with the components responsible for execution.
Worker Node에서는 아래 프로세스들이 컨테이너 실행과 네트워크 설: The following processes manage container execution and networking on a worker node.
각 Node의 **Kubelet**은 API Server에서 자신에게 배: Each Node’s **Kubelet** is an agent that checks the API Server for Pods assigned to its Node and manages their execution. When a container needs to start, it asks the **container runtime** on the same Node to run it. The runtime downloads images and actually starts or terminates container processes. Examples include containerd and CRI-O.
Kubelet이 여러 종류의 런타임에 같은 방식으로 실행을 요청할 수 있: **CRI** (Container Runtime Interface) defines the communication protocol that lets the Kubelet request execution in a consistent way across different runtimes. Through CRI, the Kubelet requests container startup and shutdown and checks execution status, then reports Pod and Node status to the API Server. [[5]](#ref-5)
1장에서 사용한 Docker Engine을 Node의 실행 기반으로 사용: When a Node uses Docker Engine, introduced in Chapter 1, **cri-dockerd** provides this connection. It is an adapter that passes the Kubelet’s CRI requests to Docker Engine in a form it can handle. With containerd, execution requests go from the Kubelet to containerd’s CRI implementation. With Docker Engine, they pass through cri-dockerd before reaching Docker Engine. [[6]](#ref-6)
**kube-proxy**는 **안정적인 진입점**(변하는 Pod 집합: **kube-proxy** implements a stable network entry point in front of changing Pods through network rules. It receives the addresses associated with that entry point and configures forwarding from the stable address to actual Pod IPs.
The **control plane** maintains desired state and makes decisions such as where Pods should run. Its main components are the API Server, Scheduler, Controller Manager, and etcd. [[7]](#ref-7)
**API Server**는 Kubernetes의 **중앙 API**입니: The **API Server** is the central Kubernetes API. kubectl and other components, including kubelets and kube-proxy, use it to query or change cluster state. It checks identity, permissions, and request validity before reflecting changes in the state store.
**etcd**는 리소스의 선언과 상태를 보관하는 데이터베이스입니다. A: **etcd** is the database holding resource declarations and state. The API Server reads and writes this store. Other components access the information through the API Server rather than accessing etcd directly.
**Scheduler**(스케줄러)는 아직 노드가 정해지지 않은 Pod를: The **Scheduler** identifies Pods that have not been assigned to a node, considers available resources and placement constraints, and selects a node. The worker node's kubelet and runtime handle container execution.
**Controller Manager**는 여러 **컨트롤러**(cont: The **Controller Manager** runs multiple **controllers**, processes that execute control loops to maintain desired state. Different controllers handle concerns such as Pod counts and node status. They Watch API resources and request corrective changes when desired and current state differ. They record changes through the API rather than logging in to nodes directly.
이 구성에서 Scheduler는 배치 위치를 결정하고, Controlle: In this arrangement, the Scheduler chooses placement, controllers request resource changes, and each kubelet manages execution on its own node.
## 5. 선언부터 Pod 실행까지의 경로: ## 5. The Path from Declaration to Pod Execution
앞에서 API, 클러스터, Control Plane, Worker Nod: We have introduced the API, cluster, control plane, and worker nodes. Now we will see how they cooperate in a single request flow to turn a declaration into running Pods and containers.
Fig 9에서 사용자가 터미널로 실행한 `kubectl`은 **kubec: In Fig 9, `kubectl` runs from the user’s terminal, reads the API Server address and credentials from **kubeconfig**, and sends an HTTPS request to that server. The following configuration connects the destination cluster with the user credentials to use.
```yaml\n# kubectl이 어느 클러스터에 어떤 사용자로 붙을지:
```yaml
# Select the cluster and user credentials for kubectl
apiVersion: v1
kind: Config
clusters:
- name: my-cluster
  cluster:
    server: https://api.my-cluster.com:6443
users:
- name: my-user
  user:
    token: <token>
contexts:
- name: my-context
  context:
    cluster: my-cluster
    user: my-user
current-context: my-context
```
- `clusters`: 접속할 클러스터의 API Server 주소를 지:
- `clusters`: API Server addresses for the available clusters.
- `users`: credentials used for authentication.
- `contexts`: connection settings that pair a cluster with a user.
- `current-context`: the name of the currently selected connection setting.
kubectl은 이 설정을 읽어 선택된 API Server에 HTTPS: kubectl reads this configuration and sends HTTPS requests to the selected API Server. [[8]](#ref-8)
선언이 Pod 실행으로 이어지는 과정을 이해하려면 상태를 저장하고 공유하: To understand how a declaration becomes a running Pod, we first need the state storage and sharing model. Kubernetes stores state, and each component subscribes to relevant changes.
위 그림은 API Server가 요청 내용을 저장하고, 각 구성요소가 W: The diagram shows the API Server storing requests and components receiving change information through Watch. We will follow a declaration that maintains a replica count and see which component observes which information. [[9]](#ref-9)
아래는 “원하는 상태를 남긴 뒤, Pod가 한 노드에서 실행될 때까지”를: The path from a desired-state declaration to execution on a node has four stages. The numbers match the diagram.
1. **사용자가 선언을 남깁니다.** kubectl이 API Serve:
1. **The user submits a declaration.** kubectl sends desired state to the API Server, which validates it and records it in **etcd**. Other components work from this stored declaration.
2. **Controllers adjust the Pod count.** Controllers in the Controller Manager Watch state changes through the API Server. When the desired and actual counts differ, they request the necessary changes, such as creating missing Pods. Those changes are also stored in etcd.
3. **The Scheduler selects a node.** It Watches for unassigned Pods, evaluates resource availability and other conditions, and records an assignment through the API Server. The assignment is stored in etcd too.
4. **The kubelet starts the containers.** The assigned node's kubelet Watches its Pods through the API Server and asks the runtime to execute their containers. Execution status returns through the API Server to etcd. The containers begin running at this stage.
이 과정에서 API에 선언이 저장된 시점과 컨테이너가 실행되는 시점은 다: Saving a declaration in the API and starting its containers happen at different times. Users must check execution and readiness separately.
이 순서는 Pod의 생성과 기동을 다룹니다. kube-proxy는 요청: This sequence covers Pod creation and startup. kube-proxy configures networking for request forwarding, so it is not included in the creation sequence.
운영에서는 API와 상태 저장소가 **한곳에만** 있으면, 그 한곳이 멈: If the API and state store exist in only one place, a failure there can disrupt cluster management. **High availability** (HA) distributes these responsibilities so that a component failure does not stop the whole system. This section introduces that structure.
Fig 12에서 사용자는 **하나의 주소**로 요청하지만, 그 뒤에는 A: In Fig 12, users send requests to **one address**, backed by three API Servers. If some fail, the remaining servers continue accepting requests. The etcd state store also usually has multiple members, often an odd number such as three. It can continue serving reads and writes while a **quorum**, or majority, remains available. Multiple worker nodes run the Pods below this control plane. This distributes control plane responsibilities across several machines rather than depending on one. [[10]](#ref-10)
이전 글에서는 Docker로 컨테이너가 종료되거나, 개수와 구성이 바뀌거: The previous article demonstrated manual recovery and changes to container count and configuration, and introduced the need for connectivity between containers. This section is not a cluster installation or execution exercise. The tables illustrate how these operational and request-routing needs translate into Kubernetes commands and declarations.
아래 표에는 **Deployment**와 **Service** 이름이 나: The tables introduce **Deployment** and **Service**. For now, think of them as a declaration that maintains the desired Pod count and a stable entry point in front of changing Pods, respectively. [[11]](#ref-11) [[12]](#ref-12)
Fig 13의 왼쪽은 중지된 컨테이너를 사람이 `docker start`: On the left of Fig 13, a person restarts a stopped container with `docker start`. On the right, deleting one of two managed Pods causes the platform to create a replacement to restore the desired count. Manually restarting a container becomes a matter of maintaining a declared set of Pods.
| Docker만 사용:
| Docker alone | Kubernetes |
| --- | --- |
| `docker stop web-server-1` `docker start web-server-1` | `kubectl delete pod <pod-name>` `kubectl get pods -l app=web` |
| **Limitation:** without a restart policy, someone must restart the container before it serves requests again. | **Improvement:** while the desired replica count remains declared, the platform restores the Pod count. |
Fig 14의 왼쪽에서는 컨테이너를 늘릴 때마다 이름과 포트를 정해 실행: On the left of Fig 14, adding containers means choosing names and ports and repeating startup commands. On the right, changing a Deployment’s desired count from two to five causes the platform to create the missing Pods. The later Service example explains how requests reach the additional Pods.
| Docker만 사용:
| Docker alone | Kubernetes |
| --- | --- |
| `docker run -d --name web-server-5 -p 8084:80 nginx:latest` `docker run -d --name web-server-6 -p 8085:80 nginx:latest` … repeated for each container and port | `kubectl scale deployment web --replicas=5` `kubectl get pods -l app=web` |
| **Limitation:** avoid port conflicts and update the frontend's target list manually. | **Improvement:** declare the Pod count without maintaining a list of host ports. |
Fig 15의 왼쪽은 컨테이너마다 중지, 삭제, 실행을 반복해 버전을 바: On the left of Fig 15, each container requires a stop, removal, and startup to change its version. On the right, setting a new image in the Deployment progressively replaces Pods, with old and new versions temporarily running together. The table uses `rollout status` to inspect progress and `rollout undo` to return to an earlier configuration.
| Docker만 사용:
| Docker alone | Kubernetes |
| --- | --- |
| `docker stop web-server-1` `docker rm web-server-1` `docker run -d --name web-server-1 -p 8080:80 nginx:1.25` … repeated per container | `kubectl set image deployment/web nginx=nginx:1.25` `kubectl rollout status deployment/web` `kubectl rollout undo deployment/web` |
| **Limitation:** updates and rollbacks are handled per container, with interruptions during replacement. | **Improvement:** changing the Deployment image progressively replaces Pods; undo restores an earlier Pod template. |
`kubectl set image`는 API에 저장된 Deployment: `kubectl set image` changes the Deployment stored in the API, not the local manifest. If files are the source of your deployment configuration, update those files too. A rollback restores a Pod template; it does not roll back database contents.
Fig 16의 왼쪽에서는 앞단의 서버 목록에 컨테이너별 주소를 적으므로,: On the left of Fig 16, a front-end server lists individual container addresses, so that list must change when containers change. On the right, clients continue using the Service name `web`, while the platform updates the target Pod information behind it. This separates a stable entry point from changing execution targets.
| Docker만 사용:
| Docker alone | Kubernetes |
| --- | --- |
| List `host:8080` … `host:8083` in the frontend configuration and restart it; use `docker inspect` to copy IPs into application settings. | `kubectl expose deployment web --port=80 --type=ClusterIP` `kubectl get svc web` |
| **Limitation:** configuration changes with container counts, and changed IPs break connections. | **Improvement:** the Service name remains stable while the platform updates its available Pod targets. |
### 7.5 배포한 컨테이너와 진입점의 삭제: ### 7.5 Removal of Workloads and Entry Points
Fig 17의 왼쪽은 실행했던 컨테이너 이름을 하나씩 찾아 삭제하는 방식: On the left of Fig 17, operators find and remove containers by name. On the right, deleting the Deployment removes its managed Pods, and separately deleting the Service removes the request entry point. The running Pod set and the way to reach it are removed through their respective declarations.
| Docker만 사용:
| Docker alone | Kubernetes |
| --- | --- |
| Repeat `docker stop …` / `docker rm …` for each name; inspect volumes and networks separately. | `kubectl delete deployment web` `kubectl delete svc web` |
| **Limitation:** track remaining containers and ports individually. | **Improvement:** remove the desired configuration at the Deployment and Service level. |
이전 글에서 반복했던 수동 복구와 스케일, 업데이트, IP 관리가, 여기: Manual recovery, scaling, updates, and address management become a model of **declaring desired state and letting the platform maintain it**.
